November 12, 2026 | 10:23 am CST
Pacific Lumber Inspection Bureau launches new curriculum
Foundations provides knowledge required for successful completion of ensuing courses, including indepth training on all the features and characteristics that impact lumber grades.

FEDERAL WAY, Wash. — Pacific Lumber Inspection Bureau (PLIB) has launched Structural Light Framing & Structural Joists and Planks. This fourth offering completes PLIB’s comprehensive grader training curriculum based on the National Grading Rule for Dimension Lumber (NGR).

“We’re pretty stoked about having completed our NGR-based curriculum,” said PLIB executive vice president Erik Wilson. “We will now begin translating these courses into different languages and focus efforts on additional grader training and other industry-focused topics as directed by PLIB members.”

Like its other online offerings, Structural Light Framing & Structural Joists and Planks is based on the in-mill grader training PLIB has offered for decades. To replicate the live training experience, PLIB’s online courses offer a wide range of learning activities, making extensive use of hundreds of close-up images, video captured from in-mill scanners and instructional videos led by PLIB’s experienced grading supervisors. The PLIB’s latest online grader training offering, Structural Light ultra-realistic learning environment helps users Framing & Structural Joists and Planks, completes the recognize and accurately measure and assess agency’s three-course series covering the NGR grades. Click every grade-defining characteristic.

While the first two offerings in this series each address a single NGR grade category, Structural Light Framing & Structural Joists and Planks addresses two different grades. “Similarities in the critical characteristics and how they impact grade in Structural Light Framing and Structural Joists and Planks allowed us to cover both grade categories in a single course, making it more efficient for those going through the training,” Wilson explained.
Structural Light Framing & Structural Joists and Planks opens with an introduction to both grade categories, followed by lessons covering the primary characteristics that determine grade -- checks, splits, shake, pockets and streaks, skip, wane, warp, slope of grain, knots and holes, and unsound wood. The course then covers manufacturing standards and grade rule Interpretations -- guidelines clarifying how grading rules apply when graders encounter lumber with unusual characteristics. Each lesson provides detailed instruction on the applicable grading rules, measurement methods and allowable limits. 3D imagery and videos shot at PLIB member mill grading stations provide learners with opportunities to apply the grading rules in realistic, practical in-mill situations. Knowledge checks at the end of each lesson reinforce the information covered, solidifying the learners’ understanding of the content.

PLIB’s four-course NGR grading curriculum accommodates a wide range of learning styles with a variety of content delivery methods, including instructional videos featuring PLIB grading supervisors, hundreds of photos depicting characteristics found in real lumber, and interactive 3-D models derived from actual in-mill scanner data. The courses are offered individually or in discounted packages. The registration fee includes personal copies of necessary course materials such as PLIB’s Grading Rule Book(s) and PLIB’s new STUD/Light Framing/Structural Light Framing/Structural Joists & Planks Dry Erase Training Wrap.
Learn more about PLIB’s education and training offerings at plib.org/lumber-gradingmarking/education-and-training/. To enroll in a course visit education.plib.org/all-courses/.
